approved: Health Insurance Amendment (Bonded Medical Programs Reform) Bill 2019
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would create a single statutory scheme to replace the current Bonded Medical Places and Medical Rural Bonded Scholarship schemes.
The scheme would require participants to work in regional, rural, remote or workforce shortage areas in return for a government-supported medical school place.
From 1 January 2020, new participants could voluntarily join the scheme, and existing participants could opt in if the Secretary agrees.
Consolidates the Bonded Medical Places and Medical Rural Bonded Scholarship schemes under one legislative framework.
Reduces the return of service obligation to three years for most new participants.
Introduces a web-portal for administrative management of the program.
Provides for internal review and Administrative Appeals Tribunal review of certain decisions.
Gives the Minister power to make Bonded Medical Program rules to keep the program up-to-date.
Medical students and doctors who accept bonded Commonwealth supported places in Australian medical courses.

The Health Insurance Amendment (Bonded Medical Programs) Reform Bill 2019 introduces a statutory Bonded Medical Program from 1 January 2020, consolidating existing schemes under a single legislative framework with $20.2 million in funding, to address doctor shortages in regional, rural and remote Australia by requiring participants to work in underserviced areas in return for a university place.

Supported the Health Insurance Amendment (Bonded Medical Programs Reform) Bill 2019, arguing that its new bonded medical program would improve access to doctors in regional, rural and remote areas while replacing two existing programs. Proposed broader workforce planning, teaching-hospital links and eligibility for outer metropolitan and Aboriginal medical services facing specialist shortages.
